content: Etravirine is a medication used in combination with other antiretroviral drugs to manage HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, allowing the immune system to function more effectively. This helps lower the risk of developing HIV-related complications, such as opportunistic infections or certain cancers, and improves overall quality of life. Etravirine is typically prescribed to individuals who have previously used other HIV medications, such as efavirenz, nevirapine, or delavirdine, which were not sufficiently effective in controlling their HIV. It belongs to a class of drugs known as non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs). However, it is important to note that etravirine is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to others, it is essential to continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Additionally, use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your healthcare provider. Avoid sharing personal items, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors, that may come into contact with blood or other bodily fluids. Take etravirine by mouth after a meal, as directed by your doctor, usually twice daily. Swallow the medication whole. If you have difficulty swallowing the tablet, you may dissolve it in a small amount of water (about 1 teaspoon or 5 milliliters). Stir the mixture well until it appears milky, then add more water, orange juice, or milk (about 1 tablespoon or 15 milliliters) and drink it immediately. Rinse the glass with additional liquid and drink it to ensure the entire dose is consumed. Repeat rinsing and drinking several times to ensure no medication is left behind. Do not use any liquid other than water to dissolve the tablet initially. It is crucial to take this medication, along with other HIV medications, exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not increase, decrease, or stop the dosage without consulting your healthcare provider, as this may reduce the effectiveness of the treatment and increase the risk of drug resistance. For optimal results, take the medication at evenly spaced intervals. Common side effects of etravirine include nausea. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. In some cases, an overactive immune response may occur, leading to symptoms. These reactions can happen at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not yet fully understood. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. However, etravirine commonly causes a mild rash, which usually appears during the second week of treatment and resolves within 1 to 2 weeks. It may be difficult to distinguish this rash from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any unusual symptoms. Before starting etravirine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. If you are pregnant, inform your doctor before using this medication. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. Etravirine passes into breast milk, so discuss breastfeeding with your doctor. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Ensure your doctor is aware of all the HIV medications you are taking, as etravirine may interact with other HIV drugs. Your doctor may need to adjust your treatment or monitor you more closely if you are taking certain combinations of HIV medications. Other drugs can affect how etravirine is removed from your body, potentially impacting its effectiveness. Examples include macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin, clarithromycin) and rifamycins (such as rifabutin, rifampin, rifapentine). If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular lab and medical tests, such as viral load and T-cell counts, should be performed to monitor your progress. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it after a meal as soon as you remember. If it is more than 6 hours after the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original bottle at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the drying agent (desiccant) in the bottle and tightly close the bottle when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
